title: Indian Ocean Thermal Expansion & Swell (1993–2025)
source: NASA MODIS Aqua SST & TOPEX/Poseidon/Jason-3/Sentinel-6 Altimetry
coords: LAT: 08.40° N | LON: 73.10° E (ARABIAN SEA / EQUATORIAL INDIAN OCEAN)
satellite: Jason-3 / MODIS Aqua / Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich

records.explanation: 1993 TOPEX/Poseidon Launch Baseline: Calm 26.8°C ocean. Low, gentle sine-wave pad.
1995: Early altimetry tracks +6.4mm steric sea level expansion.
1997 Dipole Shift: +0.5°C warming lifts ocean chord pitch; +14.2mm sea level rise.
1999 La Niña Rebound: Subsurface heat uptake continues steady upward trend.
2001 Jason-1 Calibration: Steady thermal absorption (+26.8mm). Warm mid-range frequency swell.
2003 MODIS Aqua Era: High-resolution IR radiometry confirms basin-wide warming.
2005: Sea surface nears 28°C. Faster LFO wave modulation reflects deeper swells.
2008 OSTM/Jason-2 Launch: Sea level crosses +49mm above 1993 reference ellipsoid.
2010 Marine Heatwave: 28.4°C triggers higher harmonic overtone and louder swell.
2013: Accelerated thermosteric expansion in the Arabian Sea basin.
2016 Coral Bleaching Peak: +0.5°C jump! Sharp pitch rise and heavy vibrato.
2018 Cyclone Intensification: High ocean heat content fuels rapid storm spin-up.
2020 Sentinel-6 Era: Sea level +94mm above 1993 baseline. High-energy resonant ocean chord.
2023 Global SST Anomaly: Exceeds 100mm cumulative regional sea-level rise.
2025 Critical Thermal High: 29.9°C & +112.4mm rise. Peak frequency & maximum wave pulse.
